editorial:
Imagine you are hanging out with a gritty private eye named Kiss Shiro. He is a tough guy who handles the dirty work of the city, but his world flips upside down when his own younger brother brings him a horrific rape video. From that moment, the movie turns into a dark race for justice. It feels like one of those old-school crime flicks where the atmosphere is heavy and the stakes are personal. You can tell right away that Shiro isn't just doing a job; he is fighting for his family and his own sense of right and wrong in a world that feels totally broken.

The acting is solid and keeps you hooked even when the story gets really heavy. While the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff makes it worth it. If you like stories about revenge and hard-boiled detectives, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you should try to find the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality. If you are not into discs, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to experience the grit without committing to a full purchase.
endingExplained: In the final act, Shiro tracks down the people responsible for the video. After a series of violent confrontations, he faces the main villain in a brutal showdown. Shiro manages to get his revenge, but he does not walk away happy. The movie ends with him reflecting on the cost of violence. He saves his brother from a dark path, but the trauma remains, leaving you with a sad feeling of closure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime stories and old school Japanese cinema.
